sections.content: How many people are "managers and proprietors in agriculture and horticulture"?

29,850 people

were counted on the census as "managers and proprietors in agriculture and horticulture" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Managers and proprietors in this unit group plan, organise and co-ordinate the activities and resources of farming and mixed farming establishments cultivating crops, fruits, trees and shrubs, and/or raising cattle, sheep, pigs and poultry.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "managers and proprietors in agriculture and horticulture" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 65 years or older. Of the whole working population 4.2% were aged 65 years or older. For people working as "managers and proprietors in agriculture and horticulture", 23.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "managers and proprietors in agriculture and horticulture" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "managers and proprietors in agriculture and horticulture" included:

  • company secretaries and administrators
  • undertakers, mortuary and crematorium assistants
  • clergy

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "managers and proprietors in agriculture and horticulture" there were more men than women (72.3% compared with 27.7%).

This means "managers and proprietors in agriculture and horticulture" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "other managers and proprietors".

Men made up 72.3% and women made up 27.7% of "managers and proprietors in agriculture and horticulture"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "managers and proprietors in agriculture and horticulture" included:

  • managers in logistics
  • pre-press technicians
  • chief executives and senior officials

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "managers and proprietors in agriculture and horticulture" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "managers and proprietors in agriculture and horticulture" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "managers and proprietors in agriculture and horticulture", 10.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (77.9% compared with 22.1%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (55.5%) than an employee (44.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Shropshire, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
